doc.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Joining Maynard Ferguson's band
summary: Abene joined Maynard Ferguson through Jaki Byard at about 17 and recalls the first record, the fox titles and Willie Maiden.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: It’s a good question. I think I joined at the end of ’61. I think the first record I did it was Maynard ’62 which was done at the end of ’61. And I didn’t have any charts. I think I might have had one or two charts on the first album. I don’t even remember. I try to forget some of those charts.
Was that “Three Little Foxes” that record?

That was right after that. There was so many fox numbers in, I can think of “Fox Hunt,” and there was all this fox thing going, seeping through the band over the years, you know, “Three Little Foxes,” “Three Little Foxes,” “Fox Hunt,” more foxes, less foxes, red foxes.
Willie Maiden? Was he in the band then?

Yeah. Willie was there forever I think. He was there forever. And he went on to — he became basically I saw the straw boss of Kenton’s band for a while. And it was a good scene. It was a very good scene.
